title: The Phil Hartman Story
summary: Josh and Chuck profile comedian and actor Phil Hartman, from his childhood in Brantford, Ontario and move to California, through his early comedy training, roadie and album-cover work, his Groundlings years, the Pee-wee Herman connection, his eight seasons on Saturday Night Live, his voice work on The Simpsons and News Radio, and his 1998 murder by his wife Brynn Hartman, who then killed herself. The episode closes with a listener email about drinking hot Tang.

segments.title: Opening banter and Phil Hartman introduction
segments.summary: Hosts open with Ed McMahon and Phil Hartman impressions, then introduce Hartman as an actor and comedian best known for Saturday Night Live and The Simpsons, and note his birth name spelling.

segments.title: Childhood, comedy influences and early career
segments.summary: Hartman was born in Brantford, Ontario, in 1948 and moved to Southern California as a child. He was a class clown, a surfer, and a fan of Jonathan Winters and Bob Newhart. His older brother John co-founded the management company Hartman and Goodman, which handled 1970s folk-rock acts. Phil was a roadie for Rock and Foo and designed album covers for several bands, though the hosts say the Steely Dan Aja cover rumor is false.

segments.title: First marriage, early stage work and The Music Man
segments.summary: Hartman's first marriage to Gretchen Lewis ended in divorce in 1972 after a pregnancy that ended without a child. He got his first professional stage credit as Harold Hill in The Music Man. Hosts describe his persona-driven personality and a Simpsons Lyle Lanley connection.

segments.title: Joining the Groundlings
segments.summary: The Groundlings are described as an LA sketch and improv troupe that launched many Saturday Night Live performers. Hartman reportedly performed at a Groundlings show before auditioning and joining. Tracy Newman and Lorne Michaels praised his readiness. He was known for reliability in sketches, and his Chick Hazard character is discussed. He was with the Groundlings for eleven years.

segments.title: Second marriage to Lisa Jarvis
segments.summary: Hartman married Lisa Jarvis in 1982 after a relationship following the pattern of his first marriage. They divorced in 1985.

segments.title: Pee-wee Herman and Pee-wee's Big Adventure
segments.summary: Paul Reubens developed Pee-wee Herman at the Groundlings in 1980, with Hartman contributing to writing and playing Captain Carl on Pee-wee's Playhouse. The Pee-wee show moved to the Roxy and then HBO, and Hartman co-wrote Pee-wee's Big Adventure in 1985. The documentary about Reubens is mentioned.

segments.title: Joining Saturday Night Live and rift with Reubens
segments.summary: Hartman first met Lorne Michaels when Reubens hosted Saturday Night Live in 1985. Hartman initially declined Michaels' audition offer, then later accepted and joined in 1986 with John Lovitz and other new cast members. His SNL audition is praised. Reubens reportedly became jealous and the two never reconciled.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Break before the Brynn Hartman segment.

segments.title: Meeting Brynn Amdahl and marriage
segments.summary: Hartman met Brynn Amdahl at a party in 1985, a Minnesota-born model and actress who had gotten sober. They married and had two children, Sean and Bergen. The relationship was volatile, and Brynn wanted more help with her acting career.

segments.title: SNL sketches and the Glue nickname
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Hartman's SNL characters including Phil Donahue, Ed McMahon, Frankenstein Tonto Tarzan Vin, the Little Drummer Boy sketch, Unfrozen Caveman Lawyer, and Reagan as mastermind during Iran-Contra and a Clinton impression. His nickname was the Glue, and he was in more sketches than any other cast member over eight seasons.

segments.title: Leaving SNL, film roles and News Radio
segments.summary: Hartman left SNL after eight seasons on good terms, with movie roles that were supporting rather than starring. He then starred in four seasons of News Radio as Bill McNeal.

segments.title: The Simpsons voice work: Troy McClure and Lionel Hutz
segments.summary: Hartman voiced Troy McClure and Lionel Hutz on The Simpsons starting in 1990 and continued for eight seasons. Troy McClure had a storyline with one of Marge's sisters. The hosts say the characters will not be voiced again after his death.

segments.title: Brynn Hartman's cocaine relapse and the 1998 shooting
segments.summary: Brynn relapsed after cocaine use at a News Radio Christmas party in 1997, with Andy Dick named as a source of the drug. Lovitz later blamed Dick and assaulted him in 2007. On May 27, 1998, after drinking and cocaine use, Brynn shot Phil Hartman three times while he slept. She then confessed to friends and killed herself. Their children were in the house. Phil's brother John asked mourners to forgive her.

segments.title: Aftermath, legacy and search results
segments.summary: Lovitz took over Hartman's role on News Radio, and season five opened with a character death episode. Hartman received a Walk of Fame star in 2014. Bergen and Sean were raised by their aunt Kathy and her husband. The hosts note that searches for Phil Hartman mostly return the murder and suggest looking up his SNL videos.

segments.title: Listener mail: hot Tang
segments.summary: A listener named Chris from North Georgia writes that his father served Tang hot in Ohio winters, and the hosts discuss hot Tang and similar hot drinks.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank the listener and give the show's contact and credits.
